client_frame: **Weekend added two material inputs to the Fri NFP regime shift.** First, **Berkshire Q2 is constructive-and-active**: operating earnings $12.98B (+16% YoY), net $25.7B, cash still enormous at $365.5B (down from $397B as they put money to work), buybacks reaccelerated ~20× Q1, and — most important signal — **net equity buyer for the first time in 14 quarters (~$20B)** plus post-quarter Taylor Morrison $8.5B. That is Buffett re-engaging risk after a long drought, not retreating. Second, **Iran risk reopened Saturday**: a confirmed missile strike on an ADNOC vessel undercuts the 'deal perimeters / Hormuz opening' narrative; Iran says full reopen requires US behavior change; framework still not fully signed. **Mon open cross-current**: soft NFP + Sept hold flip + Berkshire buy-signal (risk-on) versus ADNOC strike + impaired Hormuz traffic (oil/vol). VIX 14.90 into that is too calm. **Client**: (1) do not fade Berkshire's net-buy signal lightly — it's rare; (2) do not treat oil weakness as permanent after Sat's strike; (3) CPI Wed (~3.4% YoY cons) decides whether the NFP-driven hold pricing sticks; (4) NDX still −3% under June ATH — recovery not price discovery; (5) keep event vol into Wed CPI and treat Sun 6pm oil reopen as live risk.
